exposure: Pfannenstiel skin incision during cesarean hysterectomy
midline skin incision during cesarean hysterectomy
outcome: intraoperative outcomes (e.g., hypogastric artery ligation, relaparotomy, bladder injury, blood loss, blood transfusion)
postoperative outcomes (e.g., cosmetic dissatisfaction, sexual problems)
cohort: 67 women with histopathologically confirmed Placenta Accreta Spectrum Disorders who underwent cesarean section hysterectomy at Akdeniz University Hospital between January 2010 and February 2022.
finding: Pfannenstiel incisions were associated with increased risks of relaparotomy, bladder injury, blood loss, and need for blood transfusion, while midline incisions were linked to greater cosmetic dissatisfaction and sexual problems.
mod_finding: Pfannenstiel incisions during cesarean hysterectomy were associated with higher risks of surgical complications like relaparotomy and bladder injury, whereas midline incisions led to more cosmetic dissatisfaction and sexual problems.
